label: Head kill, present, my
summary: A phrase for a signature weapon's killing blow to the head or neck, in the present tense, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "shatters my jaw", "cuts my throat" and "hacks out my throat". The game's documentation says it is not valid for random choice; it does not say how an entry is picked.

label: Head kill, present, his/her
summary: The same head and neck killing blows in the present tense, but about a third person, so the text uses "his" or "her".
details: Entries: "shatters his/her jaw", "cuts his/her throat", "hacks out his/her throat". The pronoun comes from the second scope (`second`) in the text.

label: Head kill, -ing, his/her
summary: The head and neck killing blows as an -ing phrase about a third person: "shattering his/her jaw" and similar.
details: Entries: shattering the jaw, cutting the throat, hacking out the throat. The pronoun is taken from the second scope.

label: Head kill, future, my
summary: A phrase for a killing blow to the head, in the base verb form, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Four entries: "crush my skull", "cut my throat", "hack off my head" and "stab through my eye to my brain". The base form fits after words like "will" or "to".

label: Head kill, future, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the head in the base verb form, about a third person, using "his", "her" or "him".
details: Entries: crush the skull, cut the throat, hack off the head, stab in the brain. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Head kill, -ing, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the head as an -ing phrase about a third person, such as "crushing his skull" or "stabbing him in the brain".
details: Four entries: crushing the skull, cutting the throat, hacking off the head, stabbing in the brain. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Kill type, past participle
summary: A short word for how a signature weapon killed someone, in the past participle form.
details: Four entries: "crushed", "run through", "cut down" and "gutted". It has the same words as the past-tense version.

label: Kill type, past tense
summary: A short word for how a signature weapon killed someone, in the past tense.
details: Four entries: "crushed", "run through", "cut down" and "gutted". The texts are the same as in the past-participle version.

label: Rear head kill, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the back of the head in the base verb form, about a third person, using "his", "her" or "him".
details: The entry texts are "crush his/her skull", "stab him/her in the base of the skull" and "split his/her skull in two". They are in the base form, even though "Present" is in the name. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Back kill, future, my
summary: Killing blows to the back or spine in the base verb form, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "snap my spine in two", "impale my spine" and "hack my spine in two".

label: Back kill, -ing, my
summary: Killing blows to the back or spine as an -ing phrase, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "snapping my spine in two", "impaling my spine" and "hacking my spine in two".

label: Back kill, present, my
summary: Killing blows to the back or spine in the present tense ("snaps", "impales", "hacks"), with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "snaps my spine in two", "impales my spine" and "hacks my spine in two". The verb carries the -s of a third person acting; the spine is the speaker's.

label: Back kill, present, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the back or spine in the present tense, about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: snaps the spine in two, impales the spine, hacks the spine in two. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Back kill, future, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the back or spine in the base verb form, about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: snap the spine in two, impale the spine, hack the spine in two. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Back kill, -ing, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the back or spine as an -ing phrase about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: snapping the spine in two, impaling the spine, hacking the spine in two. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Kill, present, me
summary: A phrase for how a signature weapon kills the speaker, in the present tense, with the speaker as the object ("me").
details: Four entries: "crushes me", "runs me through", "cuts me down" and "guts me".

label: Kill, future, him/her
summary: How a signature weapon kills, in the base verb form, with a third person as the object ("him" or "her").
details: Entries: crush him/her, run him/her through, cut him/her down, gut him/her. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Kill, -ing, him/her
summary: How a signature weapon kills, as an -ing phrase with a third person as the object ("him" or "her").
details: Entries: crushing him/her, running him/her through, cutting him/her down, gutting him/her. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Rib wound, -ing, my
summary: A blow to the ribs as an -ing phrase, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "sliding between my ribs", "stoving in my ribs" and "hacking through my ribs". The entries are named as attack verbs, not kill types.

label: Rib wound, -ing, his/her
summary: A blow to the ribs as an -ing phrase about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: sliding between the ribs, stoving in the ribs, hacking through the ribs. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Rib wound, simple, his/her
summary: A blow to the ribs in the plain verb form about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: "stab between his/her ribs", "stove in his/her ribs", "hack through his/her ribs". The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Chest kill, future, my
summary: Killing blows to the chest in the base verb form, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "crush my sternum", "punch through my sternum" and "hew through my sternum".

label: Chest kill, -ing, my
summary: Killing blows to the chest as an -ing phrase, with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "crushing my sternum", "punching through my sternum" and "hewing into my sternum".

label: Chest kill, present, my
summary: Killing blows to the chest in the present tense ("crushes", "punches", "hews"), with the victim speaking as "my".
details: Three entries: "crushes my sternum", "punches through my sternum" and "hews into my sternum".

label: Chest kill, present, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the chest in the present tense, about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: crushes the sternum, punches through the sternum, hews into the sternum. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Chest kill, future, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the chest in the base verb form, about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: crush the sternum, punch through the sternum, hew through the sternum. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Chest kill, -ing, his/her
summary: Killing blows to the chest as an -ing phrase about a third person, using "his" or "her".
details: Entries: crushing the sternum, punching through the sternum, hewing into the sternum. The pronoun comes from the second scope.

label: Weapon name or type
summary: Either the signature weapon's own name or its general type.
details: The name entry reads the artifact stored in the variable `signature_weapon_scope` on the root and prints its name. The type entry prints the root character's `signature_weapon` custom text instead. The input does not show how one of the two is chosen.

label: Weapon tip adjective
summary: An adjective for the tip of a signature weapon: "sharp" or "heavy".

label: Weapon tip part
summary: The word "point", "head" or "edge", for the working part of a signature weapon.

label: Wound verb 1
summary: An attack verb in the plain form, the first of several groups: "hew", "smash" or "stab".
details: The -ing and third-person versions are separate custom texts.

label: Wound verb 1, -ing
summary: The first group of wound verbs as an -ing word: "hewing", "smashing" or "stabbing".

label: Wound verb 1, he/she form
summary: The first group of wound verbs in the form that follows he or she: "hews", "smashes" or "stabs".

label: Wound verb 2
summary: A second group of wound verbs in the plain form: "bite", "crack" or "puncture".

label: Wound verb 2, -ing
summary: The second group of wound verbs as an -ing word: "biting", "cracking" or "puncturing".

label: Wound verb 2, he/she form
summary: The second group of wound verbs in the form that follows he or she: "bites", "cracks" or "punctures".

label: Wound verb 3
summary: A third group of wound verbs in the plain form: "rend", "annihilate" or "skewer".

label: Wound verb 4
summary: A fourth group of wound verbs in the plain form: "carve", "mangle" or "chop".

label: Wound verb 4, he/she form
summary: The fourth group of wound verbs in the form that follows he or she: "carves", "mangles" or "chops".

label: Wound verb 5
summary: A fifth group of wound verbs in the plain form: "plunge" or "drive".

label: Wound verb 5, -ing
summary: The fifth group of wound verbs as an -ing word: "plunging" or "driving".

label: Wound verb 5, he/she form
summary: The fifth group of wound verbs in the form that follows he or she: "plunges" or "drives".

label: Wound verb 6, -ing
summary: A sixth group of wound verbs as an -ing word: "cutting" or "smashing".

label: Sinful trait
summary: The name of a personality trait, taken from a fixed list of vice and virtue traits such as lustful, chaste, greedy and generous.
details: The list holds 35 traits in all, in pairs, for example lustful and chaste, greedy and generous, wrathful and calm, plus ones like cynical, zealous and sadistic. The input shows texts only for the first four: Lustful, Chaste, Gluttonous, Temperate.

label: Sister or brother
summary: The word "sister" or "brother".
details: The entries are the relation words `relation_sister` and `relation_brother`. The input does not say how one is chosen.

label: Sister's or brother's
summary: The possessive "sister's" or "brother's".

label: Sisterhood or brotherhood
summary: The word "sisterhood" or "brotherhood".

label: Sisters or brothers
summary: The plural word "sisters" or "brothers".

label: Small animal
summary: The name of a small animal such as a rabbit, squirrel, bird or mouse.
details: The list has five entries; the fifth is keyed as a hedgehog (its text is not shown). The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Small animals, plural
summary: The plural name of a small animal: rabbits, squirrels, birds and mice, plus a fifth keyed as hedgehogs.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice. The hedgehog text itself is not shown, only its key.

label: Farm animal with sound
summary: A farm animal with its sound as an -ing word, such as "bleating goat" or "clucking chicken".
details: Eight entries keyed as goat, chicken, cow, sheep, pig, yak, camel and horse (for example "bellowing cow", "whinnying horse"). The animal name in each text is pulled in from a separate `regional_farm_animal_...` text key. The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Stammer letter m or f
summary: The letter "m" or "f".
details: Going by the name, it is the repeated first letter of a stammered "mother" or "father"; the input shows no use.

label: Kind of vassals
summary: A word for a kind of vassals: nobility, clan, chieftains, the faith's priests or citizenry.
details: The clergy entry prints the plural alternative priest term of the character's faith. All five entries are keys of the statecraft event 4010.

label: Ancestor stele text
summary: The inscription on a stele (carved stone) that honors a dead ancestor, with a variant per kind of person.
details: 90 entries in all. The ones listed include a generic one, one for a child who died young, and ones for a diplomat, a family-first person, a reveler, a blademaster, a hunter and so on. Each starts with a shared intro text and ends with a shared carver text. Some entries speak of the person as "he" or "she", taken from the variable `stele_container`. The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Conquest stele text
summary: The inscription on a stele that celebrates a conquest, with a variant for how the war went.
details: Five entries: bloody, glorious, hard fought, embarrassingly easy and often forgotten. Each begins with a shared intro text and ends with a shared carver text. The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Promotion stele text
summary: The inscription on a stele for someone taking power, such as predestined, truly worthy, magnificent, awe-inspiring or majestic.
details: Five entries, each with a shared intro text and a shared carver text. Some use "he" or "she" or "his/her" for the person who ordered the stele (variable `stele_commissioner`). The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Strongest AI value
summary: A noun for a personality drive, such as boldness, kind heart, selfishness or energy.
details: 16 nouns in all (12 listed), including honor, rationality, vindictive nature, ardent belief, caution, coldness, lack of ambition and lethargy, named by their keys. Going by the name, it names the character's strongest AI value; the input does not show how that is chosen. The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Study: offices word
summary: A word for religious services: "the offices", "the daily prayers" or "the daily rites".
details: The entries share the key prefix `pam_ss_word_`; the input does not show what picks one.

label: Study: parish word
summary: A word for the group a priest looks after: "parish" or "congregation".

label: Study: pulpit word
summary: A word for the place a preacher speaks from: "pulpit", "minbar" or "lectern".

label: Study: seminary word
summary: A word for a place of religious schooling: "seminary", "madrasa" or "school".

label: Subject standing concept
summary: A clickable game-concept link to either imperial grace or subject standing.
details: The entries produce concept links, not plain words. The imperial grace entry appears twice in the list; subject standing once.

label: Subject standing icon
summary: The imperial grace icon, or nothing.
details: Two entries give the imperial grace icon; the last one gives empty text. This is probably the matching icon for the concept text above, but the input does not say so.

label: Imperial grace loss text
summary: A sentence telling how much imperial grace all celestial tributaries (the game's term) lose each year in the current phase of the dynastic cycle.
details: Six entries, one per phase: stability, stability expansion, stability advancement, instability, instability conquest and chaos. The amount comes from a script value named for the phase. The instability entry names the stability advancement phase in its text, which looks like a copy slip in the game's text.

label: Suitable gift
summary: The name of an item that works as a gift, such as a saddle, gown, jacket or dagger.
details: Twelve items in all, among them a sword, a silver inkhorn, a ruby ring, an emerald necklace, an enamel brooch, a tapestry and a leatherbound journal (named by their keys). The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Survey: control line
summary: A bullet line in the survey arrival text that tells the player to improve control, with the current value; empty when control is maxed.
details: The value comes from the script value `survey_province_control_info_value`. The bad entry shows it in the negative color, the neutral one in yellow, the maxed entry gives nothing.

label: Survey: development line
summary: A bullet line in the survey arrival text that tells the player to improve development, with the current value; empty when development is maxed.
details: The value comes from `survey_province_development_info_value`. Good is shown in the positive color, bad in the negative color, neutral in yellow.

label: Survey: opinion line
summary: A bullet line in the survey arrival text that tells the player to improve opinion, showing what the second character thinks of the player.
details: Shown in the positive or negative color, or empty. The number is the second scope's opinion of the player.

label: Survey: popular opinion line
summary: A bullet line in the survey arrival text that tells the player to improve county opinion, with the current value.
details: The value comes from `survey_province_popular_opinion_info_value`. It is shown in the positive, negative or yellow color. The maxed entry still prints a line, in the positive color.

label: Survey: old building
summary: A short phrase naming an old piece of infrastructure the survey finds in a province, such as old farms, castle walls or an old mayor's house.
details: Five entries: farm, castle, city, temple and manors. Each text ends in "in". The temple entry names the county faith's house of worship. It runs on a province and the game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Teaching response
summary: A short reply to a teaching, with a variant per political movement in the dynastic cycle.
details: Six entries: pro-hegemon, expansion, advancement, conservative, undecided and a fallback. Each is a gentle objection in the same style as the matching teaching text.

label: Teaching text
summary: A short wise saying, with a variant per political movement in the dynastic cycle.
details: Six entries: pro-hegemon, expansion, advancement, conservative, undecided and a fallback. The answer text is in a paired custom text.

label: Terrain inspiration
summary: A poetic phrase describing a landscape, such as lofty mountain peaks or rolling hills.
details: Eleven entries, one per terrain: mountains, hills, jungle, taiga, wetlands, floodplains, desert, forest, farmlands, steppe and drylands. It runs on a province.

label: Terrain struggle
summary: A phrase about harsh weather: through a thick snowfall, through torrential rain or beneath the beating sun.
details: Three entries, keyed winter, rain and sun.

label: Terrain name
summary: The name of a terrain type in plain words, such as plains, hills or mountains.
details: Thirteen terrains in all, for example farmlands, desert, oasis, jungle, forest, taiga, wetlands, steppe and floodplains (named by their keys). It runs on a character.

label: Terrain name of a county
summary: The name of a terrain type, written for a title (county) instead of a character.
details: It has the same terrain keys as the character version, such as plains, farmlands, hills and mountains, and runs on a landed title.

label: Terrain name, county, plural
summary: The plural name of a terrain type, written for a title (county), such as plains, deserts, oases, forests or steppes.
details: Thirteen terrains in all. Some keys are plural forms of the singular ones, like deserts, oases, jungles, taigas.

label: Terrain name of a province
summary: The name of a terrain type, written for a province.
details: Fourteen terrains in all, with words like plains, farmlands, hills and mountains. It runs on a province.

label: Terrain prefix
summary: An adjective to put before a terrain name: verdant, rolling, mighty, endless, lush or rich.
details: It runs on a province.

label: Artifact type word
summary: A plain word for the kind of artifact meant, such as crown, weapon, armor or regalia.
details: There are 32 types in all, including trinket, big wall piece, small wall piece, throne, sculpture, book, pedestal and elixir (named by their keys). The helmet type reads as "crown" and the primary armament as "weapon".

label: This is you
summary: A line saying "This is you" with a twist: allegedly, unfortunately, not always feeling like yourself or magnificent.
details: Five entries; the fifth is a key entry whose text is not shown in the input.

label: Number three to twelve
summary: A number written as a word, from three to twelve.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice, with ten entries.

label: Number three to twelve, instrumental
summary: The numbers from three to twelve in a special instrumental form; the input gives no text for them.
details: Ten entries, all with a text key but no shown text. The game does not state in this data what instrumental form means here.

label: Throwable object
summary: A thing someone could throw, with its article: a shoe, an empty cup, a stick or a rock.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Title adjective base
summary: Probably a building block for the adjective form of a title name; the input shows no text for its entries.
details: Four entries, keyed for no tier, Francia, a default and a fallback. It runs on a title.

label: Title adjective base 2
summary: Probably a second building block for the adjective form of a title name; the input shows no text for its one entry.
details: The single entry is keyed for titles with no tier. It runs on a title.

label: Title is plural
summary: Probably a yes or no marker for whether a title name is a plural; the input shows no text.
details: Two entries, keyed true and false. It runs on a title.

label: Title rank concept
summary: Probably a game concept link for the rank of a title (barony, county, duchy, kingdom, empire); the input shows no text.
details: Five entries, one per rank, each a concept key ending in `_pos`. It runs on a title.

label: Title and owner relation
summary: A line naming a title and whose it is: "Your title" or "[relation]'s title".
details: Five entries: your primary title, your title, the holder's primary title, the holder's title, and a none case. For other holders the text names the holder by their relation to you. The four texts shown end with a line break.

label: Title Z or Ze
summary: Two text keys, `title_ze` and `title_z`, for a title; the input shows no text.
details: It runs on a title. The names suggest a letter ending, but the input does not confirm it.

label: Faith tolerance word
summary: A word for how a faith is regarded: righteous, astray, hostile or evil.
details: The entry keyed sinister reads "hostile".

label: Faith tolerance adjective
summary: The adjective form of the faith tolerance words (righteous, astray, hostile, evil); the input shows no text.

label: Faith tolerance concept
summary: A link to the game concept for how a faith is regarded: righteous, astray, hostile or evil.
details: The entries produce clickable links.

label: Regent or imperial family
summary: A link to the concept regent family or imperial family.
details: Going by its name, it says which kind of family the top liege belongs to; the input shows no use.

label: Town crier notice A
summary: An announcement shouted by a town crier, such as a call for adventurers for a treasure hunt, escort work or discreet experts.
details: Nine entries for different kinds of offered work (treasure map, transport, criminal, justicar, hireling, diplomacy, stewardship, learning and intrigue contracts), all keys of event ep3_laamp_decision_event.1025. The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice. Options B and C list the same entries.

label: Town crier notice B
summary: A second announcement slot of the town crier, with the same entries as notice A.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice. Having a separate slot presumably lets a second notice differ from the first; the input does not show that.

label: Town crier notice C
summary: A third announcement slot of the town crier, with the same entries as notices A and B.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice. Having a separate slot presumably lets a third notice differ from the others; the input does not show that.

label: Town crier reply A
summary: A quoted spoken line in reply to a town crier notice, such as "A treasure hunt, you say?".
details: Ten entries, keys of the option texts of event ep3_laamp_decision_event.1025: one for a legendary noble, and nine matching the notice kinds (treasure map, transport, criminal, justicar and so on). The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Town crier reply B
summary: A second reply slot for the town crier, with the same entries as reply A.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Town crier reply C
summary: A third reply slot for the town crier, with the same entries as replies A and B.
details: The game's documentation marks it as valid for random choice.
